messages:
sre-oncall: Heads up — eu1 apiserver is seeing ~40% conn resets over the last 5m, controller-manager restarted twice, etcd leader lease renewals spiking after a GPU pool scale event.
ashley: got it, any correlated alerts from net/egress?
raj: yes, NAT SNAT exhaustion alert popped at 09:12UTC for eu1-b. A bunch of GPU nodes were deprovisioned then reattached causing many ephemeral connections to churn.
maria: logs show a flood of watch reconnects from kube-proxy: 
```
E0409 09:12:27.123 kube-proxy.go:453] failed to proxy: dial tcp 10.20.7.12:6443: connection reset by peer
```
ashley: which autoscaler triggered the deprovision? aws-gpu-autoscale policy?
raj: yes, policy TTL-based scale-down + a bursty batch job that then requeued and rehydrated nodes.
sre-oncall: suspected chain: scale-down -> conntracking entries freed/recreated -> SNAT pool pressure -> apiserver connections reset -> apiserver watchers flood reconnects -> controller-manager backoff -> brief leader renewal jitter on etcd.
tyler: can we confirm conntrack exhaustion? infra-bot: conntrack_count eu1-b = 97500 / 100000 (threshold 90%) :warning:
maria: also seeing a small nvme io spike on control plane nodes around the same time, not huge but might have amplified latencies for etcd fsyncs.
ashley: plan: 1) pause GPU autoscaler for eu1 for 15m, 2) bump conntrack and SNAT ephemeral port range, 3) increase apiserver keepalive timeout to avoid aggressive resets, 4) failover etcd leader if leader is on the noisy node.
raj: executing step 1 now — scaling policy set to "hold".
tyler: doing conntrack sysctl bump on kube-proxy nodes: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` (will roll via daemonset).
ashley: Maria, can you check etcd leader location and health?
maria: etcdctl endpoint status shows leader on eu1-b-03 and follower latencies elevated (avg commit 28ms -> 120ms during spike). Will set leader-election-ttl temporarily lower? not ideal.
sre-oncall: i'd prefer leader move — try safe failover: mark eu1-b-03 unsched and wait for leader to step down.
raj: cordoning eu1-b-03 now, will monitor for graceful leader transfer.
ashley: added a short canary route to redirect critical control plane traffic to eu1-a region to reduce load on eu1-b.
infra-bot: deploybot: route-update applied to control-plane-balancer (canary -> eu1-a) :white_check_mark:
maria: leader moved to eu1-a-01 after cordon, commit latency dropped back to ~30ms. etcd health ok.
tyler: conntrack pressure dropping to 45% after sysctl + holding autoscaler.
sre-oncall: apiserver reset rate down to baseline, controller-manager stable. Watching for 30m.
raj: follow-up actions: - revert autoscaler hold after 30m gradual scale-up window, - harden autoscaler cooldown for GPU pools, - add conntrack backpressure metric alert, - add probe to detect rapid scale-down/up cycles.
ashley: will open a follow-up RFC for safer GPU scale policies (cooldown + drain-check for long-living apiserver clients).
maria: adding an eval to Redwood Optimize: flag workloads that cause rapid churn for GPU nodes.
tyler: taking ownership of conntrack alert tuning.
sre-oncall: thanks team. tagging ENG-PLATFORM and PRODUCT to sync on cost vs safety tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
ashley: quick note — customer-facing latency blips were ~200ms extra during event, no API failures reported. Logging incident for postmortem.
raj: documenting runbook changes in infra runbooks/gpu-autoscale.md after postmortem.
sre-oncall: closing thread when metrics stable. :eyes:
__notes: This document is a single Slack thread in eng-sre about an apiserver/etcd/controller-manager disruption tied to GPU autoscaler churn and conntrack/SNAT pressure.
